name: Tuscarora
catalog_quote: In Chitimacha, a language of the Gulf, the main stress always occurs on the first syllable of a word, while in Tuscarora, a Northern Iroquoian language, it occurs on the next-to-last (penultimate) syllable.

audit.recode_to: Keep penultimate as the fixed position; add the documented exceptions (epenthetic joiner -a- in the penult is skipped -> antepenultimate stress; imperatives may carry final stress; Rudes 1999: word-stress 'may fall on the ultimate, penultimate, or antepenultimate syllable'). If the catalog's 'strict' flag is meant to exclude such morphophonemically conditioned displacements, Tuscarora should move to fixed-dominant together with Mohawk and Onondaga, which the catalog currently codes fixed-strict with the same caveat in their quotes.
audit.deciding_source_kind: database or survey citing another work

sources.quote: '...although the normal stres[s] placement in Tuscarora is penultimate, a penultimate syllable cannot receive the stress if it contains a morphophonemically epenthetic vowel -- indicated by -(a)-. Normally in such cases, the stress falls on the antepenult. However, in the rare case where both the penultimate and antepenultimate syllables contain epenthetic vowels, then the stress falls on the penultimate as in [...]'. Also: 'The prothetic /i/ ... is there to supply a penultimate syllable for stress placement purposes, since verb forms, except for imperatives, cannot be stressed on the ultimate

sources.quote: '...when spoken in isolation, has only one word-stress, which may fall on the ultimate, penultimate, or antepenultimate syllable (Rudes, 1995).' Underlined-vowel convention: 'the vowel in question behaves exceptionally with respect to stress placement. If it occurs in the penultimate syllable, and is not preceded by another underlined vowel, it is skipped over by the stress, which instead falls on the antepenultimate syllable; if it occurs in a penultimate syllable and is preceded by another underlined vowel, then it receives the stress.'
sources.locator: Introduction (roman-numbered pages, section on the word and orthographic conventions); exact page not recoverable from snippets
sources.note: States that word-stress 'may fall on the ultimate, penultimate, or antepenultimate syllable' and gives the explicit rule for epenthetic (underlined) vowels being skipped by penultimate stress — the exception our 'fixed-strict' record does not mention; full pages needed to pin the locator and the default-rule sentence.
